items.title: Don Smedley and Tom Stagg Interview, 1969-10-03
items.q: Before Nelson was due to return home to the States, before he went, the day before he went, we did a recording with the Barry Martin rhythm section... and Lewis Nelson on trombone.

ctx.x: May I interrupt? Would you come from... come from, uh... the, uh... perhaps... 1949, the, uh, Ken Collier, the Queen River? You come from there. Yeah.

Ken Collier came back from New Orleans in, in, in late 1953, and this altered really the whole aspect of traditional jazz in England. The first thing he did was to, to get together the finest of the traditional musicians of that time in the country, and, um, he chose Chris Barber on his rumbum. Before that, for a very short period, a fellow called Ed MacDonald, who came from the north of England. He used Chris Barber and Dizz Disley on guitar, and banjo at that time. And these were the finest musicians of, of…
Now may I ask you, from where is Barry Martin spring?
